//: Lighthouse CI over the static export (Issue #60). `staticDistDir` makes LHCI serve out/ itself, so no dev server and no auth are involved. Only API-free routes are audited: the (app) group calls the API on mount, and with no API in CI the liveness probe escalates and `navigateToUnavailable` sends the audit to /unavailable — which then 404s, because the export writes that page as out/unavailable.html while out/unavailable/ exists as an RSC-payload directory with no index.html. Auditing /lobby, /table or /hands here therefore measures a redirect, not the page. Per-route first-load JS for those routes is covered deterministically by `npm run bundle:check`, which needs no browser; what Lighthouse adds is real render metrics, and it can only get those where the page actually renders. Category scores on a shared runner move by a few points between runs, so they are asserted as warnings; the resource budgets below are deterministic and are the hard gate.
